confirmed.claim: Marked crossing-curve length is not invariant on the pants-twist quotient.
confirmed.proof_or_limited_counterexample: The matrices A=[[1,1],[1,2]], B=[[1,-1],[-1,2]] realize a complete once-punctured Markoff torus; detA=detB=1, trA=trB=trAB=3, trA^2B=6, tr[A,B]=-2. The crossing curve b has distinct lengths 2acosh(3/2) and2acosh(3) at X and its squared pants twist, which represent one quotient point. This marked crossing-curve function does not descend; pants-curve functions are not ruled out.
confirmed.counterevidence: Pants curves and twist-invariant classes descend. Pants twists permute the set C of all node-crossing curves, so the collective condition ell_gamma>M for every gamma in C does descend. The already-invoked collar lemma supplies uniform local control near a node.
confirmed.core_impact: The individual-function assertion is false, but the collective condition used in Proposition4.1 is twist invariant and has local control from the existing collar lemma. No missing central continuity premise or continuity counterexample is established.
confirmed.repair_boundary: Restrict individual global functions to invariant data or local marked lifts; formulate the crossing-curve condition collectively. The existing collar lemma bounds all crossing lengths uniformly near nodes, and normalized components control other short curves.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: For the retained complete punctured Markoff torus, A=[[1,1],[1,2]] and B=[[1,-1],[-1,2]] have determinant one, traces A=B=AB=3 and commutator trace -2. A^2 B=[[-1,4],[-2,7]] has trace 6. Thus the simple marked crossing curve b has lengths 2 arcosh(3/2) and 2 arcosh(3) on two markings identified by the pants twist quotient. That individual function does not descend.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: Pants lengths and twist-invariant curve classes do descend. More decisively, Proposition 4.1 uses the collection C of all curves crossing a node. Pants twists permute C, so the simultaneous lower-bound predicate is invariant. The collar lemma already invoked on p.17 gives a uniform bound for all crossing curves near sufficiently short finitely many nodal pants curves; normalized components handle the rest.
independent_verification.repair_check: Restrict the individual-function statement to invariant curves or a marked local lift. Preserve the actual collective argument; the finding does not establish a missing core continuity assumption or a counterexample to tropicalization continuity.

confirmed.claim: Completed standard grt1 cannot be identified with or injected into the printed all-genus direct sums.
confirmed.proof_or_limited_counterexample: Standard grt1 is the solution space of homogeneous linear equations in completed Lie series. Nonzero homogeneous odd sigma_(2j+1) give an injection Q^N -> grt1 by formal sums. Hence domain uncountable. Direct sum of finite-dimensional W0Hc groups is countable. HMod_g is countable; its rational bar complexes and homology are countable-dimensional; their countable direct sum is a countable set. Thus no set injection from the standard completed algebra to either printed direct sum exists.
confirmed.counterevidence: Surrounding genus-graded language plausibly intends the direct-sum graded subalgebra. Every fixed-genus assertion is unaffected.
confirmed.core_impact: Literal all-genus statements need convention/completion correction; finite-genus injection and main geometric model not refuted.
confirmed.repair_boundary: Define grt1^gr as the direct sum of weight components, or replace targets by products and extend degreewise. State the topology/completion.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The cited completed grt_1 admits independently varying rational coefficients of nonzero homogeneous sigma_(2j+1), hence an uncountable Q^N family. A direct sum of finite-dimensional genus cohomology groups is countable as a set. The stated handlebody target is also countable-dimensional over Q, since the countable group has a countable rational bar complex. The complete product cannot inject into these literal direct sums.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The surrounding argument is degreewise and finite-genus. The graded direct-sum Lie algebra gives the intended statement; alternatively both sides may be consistently completed. No fixed-genus class or principal geometric statement is refuted.
independent_verification.repair_check: Specify the graded rather than completed algebra, or use product targets and the completed degreewise map.

confirmed.location: Corollary1.6 critical-base estimate and its free-Lie derivation
confirmed.claim: The displayed free-Lie lower bound does not imply the printed endpoint normalization.
confirmed.proof_or_limited_counterexample: For ordinary weight-graded free Lie L on one generator each odd degree>=3, a_n=dimL_n and PBW gives product(1-t^n)^(-a_n)=(1-t^2)/(1-t^2-t^3). If beta is the positive root ofr^3-r-1 and P_n is the sum of nth powers of its3 roots, then n*a_n=sum_(d|n)mu(d)(P_(n/d)-2*[n/d even]). Other roots have modulus beta^(-1/2), giving a_n~beta^n/n. Hence beta^(-n)a_n->0, while n*beta^(-n)a_n->1. The integer model B_n=a_n satisfies the lower-bound mechanism but violates the stated normalization; it is not asserted to equal actual handlebody Betti numbers.
confirmed.counterevidence: Actual handlebody homology may contain extra classes. The cited CGP statements require any base strictly smaller than beta; nonvanishing and exponential growth remain supported.
confirmed.core_impact: Corollary1.6 is a quantitative consequence of the central genus-graded injection on p6. The supplied free-Lie lower bound does not establish the critical-base normalization, making this a Major invalid quantitative derivation. The actual endpoint Betti inequality is unresolved; no full Betti-sequence counterexample is claimed.
confirmed.repair_boundary: Use dimH>=a_n~beta^n/n, or liminf n beta^(-n)dimH>=1, or every base1<b<beta. Retaining stronger endpoint needs new control of additional classes.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The free Lie algebra with one generator in each odd degree >=3 has PBW identity product_(g>=1)(1-t^g)^(-a_g)=(1-t^2)/(1-t^2-t^3). Taking logarithms and Mobius inversion gives a_g~beta^g/g, where beta^3-beta-1=0. Thus beta^(-g)*a_g tends to zero, while g*beta^(-g)*a_g tends to one. A lower bound B_g>=a_g alone cannot imply the printed liminf beta^(-g)*B_g>=1.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The source presents Corollary 1.6 as the quantitative consequence of the central genus-graded injection. The cited CGP result uses every base strictly below beta and retains the divisor g. Additional handlebody classes could make actual Betti numbers larger, so a_g is a countermodel to the inference, not an asserted actual Betti sequence.
independent_verification.repair_check: Retain B_g>=a_g, liminf g*beta^(-g)*B_g>=1 and exponential growth for any smaller base, or supply additional independent information for the stronger endpoint. Surviving nonvanishing and qualitative exponential growth do not reduce this quantitative core derivation failure.
